🇲🇽🗿 <u>62 YEARS OF THE PALACE THAT GUARDS MEXICO’S SOUL</u>

The Museo Nacional de Antropología turns 62 — 42,000 m² and 24 halls built expressly to hold Mexico’s memory, from the Aztec Sun Stone on down. It’s the crown of a country that now runs 1,739 museums, 197 in the capital alone, free for everyone every Sunday and always free for students, seniors and kids. Commissioned by López Mateos and designed by Pedro Ramírez Vázquez, it was built — unlike borrowed colonial palaces — to be a museum: a nation choosing to house its own history.

⚽🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO’S ANTITRUST COP GOES AFTER LIGA MX</u>

Mexico’s antitrust commission (CNA) has opened a formal investigation (IO-001-2026) into Liga MX for scrapping promotion and relegation — permanently locking second-division clubs like Leones Negros and Mineros out of the top flight in a business that moves over 52 billion pesos and 150,000 jobs a year. League boss Francisco Iturbide claims smaller clubs “lack the economic solvency to move up”; regulators can fine the guilty up to 10% of annual revenue. In 2021 the same clubs and the FMF were already fined 177.6 million pesos for collusion.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>1810 WAS A COGNITIVE WAR — AND SO IS 2026</u>

Writing in Contralínea, philosopher Fernando Buen Abad argues Mexico’s Independence began as a battle over perception, not just muskets: before any political structure falls, he writes, the collective belief that sustains it must first lose its effectiveness. Napoleon’s 1808 invasion of Spain cracked colonial legitimacy; Hidalgo’s 1810 call was an intervention on collective perception. Two centuries later the battlefield is algorithmic — but the target is the same: what a people believe is possible.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>SHEINBAUM WON’T ANNOUNCE A DEAL UNTIL IT’S FINAL</u>

After a call with Trump on Wednesday, Sheinbaum told her Guanajuato mañanera that trade talks are “going well” — but refused to announce anything: “until the final agreement is in place, we couldn’t announce it.” A fresh negotiating round opens Sept 28–29 in Washington, with Foreign Minister Velasco and Economy Secretary Ebrard at the table. No premature victory lap.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO & CANADA DEEPEN TIES WHILE TRUMP THREATENS</u>

One year into the Sheinbaum–Carney Action Plan, Mexico and Canada are building the trade architecture Washington keeps threatening to blow up. A single Team Canada mission brought 244 Mexican businesspeople into more than 1,000 meetings with Canadian firms, and both governments are now coordinating on critical minerals, ports, clean energy and supply-chain security ahead of the 2026 T-MEC review.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Even Fitch calls Mexico's 2027 budget "more credible"</u>

Fitch Ratings said Mexico's 2027 economic package is "more credible" than previous ones, crediting new revenue measures and more realistic assumptions — the agency's own 1.8% growth estimate now sits just below Hacienda's 2% midpoint. Fitch still flags risks: it wants the broad deficit near 2.5% of GDP to stabilize debt, and names Pemex's unfinished refining recovery. Coverage via El Economista — a notable shift from an agency that spent years warning of fiscal drift.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>China defends Mexico's sovereignty after US embassy mocks its Independence Day</u>

When the US embassy posted "Viva México, Made in China" to jab at Mexico on its Independence Day, China's embassy fired back, accusing Washington of "sowing discord" by using a patriotic celebration to attack a third country. "A sovereign state has every right to independently choose its partners," it said, invoking four centuries of Mexico-China trade dating to the Nao de China. Cooperation, it added, will hold steady despite the attacks.

🇲🇽💊 <u>Veracruz commits 1 billion pesos to medicines and 1,300 new clinics</u>

Governor Rocío Nahle announced 1 billion pesos for medicines and health supplies across Veracruz's 212 municipalities, plus 1,300 first-contact clinics built through the IMSS-Bienestar agreement. Sixty ambulances arrive in 2026 and another 60 in 2027, with medicine hauled to rural communities by the state's "Health Vans." "We'll buy everything needed through IMSS-Bienestar and distribute it by regional need," Nahle said.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Foreign investment hits record $40.8 billion in Sheinbaum's second year</u>

Foreign direct investment reached a historic $40.871 billion in 2025, up 10.8% from 2024 — and Q1 2026 already logged $23.591 billion, up 10.4% year-on-year. Nearly 60% came from the US, Spain and Canada, flowing into semiconductors, clean energy, vehicle manufacturing and finance. The government reported that the flows "reaffirmed investors' confidence" in Mexico's macroeconomic stability and T-MEC integration — the nearshoring bet landing while the doomsayers kept forecasting capital flight.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum to Trump: no one judges Mexico from the outside</u>

After Trump's proclamation branding Mexico a drug-transit country and demanding it arrest officials tied to organized crime, Sheinbaum didn't blink: "We don't need to be judged from outside — we know Mexico's problems, we act on them every day, and we report it." She added she'd like to see a report on what the US itself does. Her government has moved against organized crime and against public servants colluding with it, with results published daily — no foreign proclamation required.
